LEFT panel morning sunlight, calm pond: water surface clearly BELOW a bold horizontal reference mark on pillar. RIGHT panel evening after rain, low warm sky, wet bank: water surface clearly ABOVE that identical bold reference mark. Put the bold mark at precisely the same vertical position in both panels, visible in right panel through shallow clear water; other tick marks are thinner and evenly spaced, identical on both pillars. Both banks and pillars stay fixed; only waterline and time-of-day lighting change. No numbers, words, titles, equations, arrows with quantities, real place names or answer. Both levels and reference line must stay readable in grayscale, do not use color alone. Keep water below the left reference and above the right reference; no ambiguity. This is qualitative comparison, not a precise measurement diagram. Style: Warm watercolor and editorial ink, restrained soft colors, crisp important outlines.
